**Finding re-submitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The verifier's substantive review confirmed the analysis on every point, so this pass was a clean-up rather than a change of position:

- Fixed a typo in the rationale and tightened the wording.
- Added one genuine residual check: the integration clause (14.10) incorporates the separate Non Disclosure Agreement and Statement of Work, neither of which is in this file. We should confirm from the deal record that neither carries a personnel covenant — that is the only route by which a non-solicit could reach Corio.
- Retained the note that the failed deterministic checks (12-month duration, general-solicitation carve-out) are fallback parameters and are inapplicable where no restrictive covenant exists.

Position on the rule is unchanged: nothing in this Agreement restricts Corio from soliciting or employing Commerce One personnel, which satisfies the preferred position, so the finding is internal evidence only. If Commerce One later raises a personnel covenant, we hold to the fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
